children.name: Reading is a slow activity, and that is the point. Every reader worth keeping gives the words room.

A quiet page is not an empty one. It is a page that has made up its mind about what it is for, and then removed everything else. The margins do most of the work: they hold the text away from the edges of the window the way a frame holds a picture, and in doing so they tell you where to look.

Typography is the whole interface here. There is no toolbar to reach for, no chrome to decode, no icon that needs a tooltip. The size of the letters, the space between the lines, and the length of the measure are the only controls that matter, and they are all set once and then left alone.
Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity.

A line of type wants somewhere between sixty and seventy-five characters. Shorter and the eye jumps too often; longer and it loses the next line on the way back. Folio's measure is fixed at seven hundred and twenty points for exactly this reason.
Serif for prose, sans for the frame.
A progress bar three points tall, and no more.
